title: Behind the Mask: Masking, Autistic Burnout, and Suicide Risk in Autistic Women
content: Masking has been associated with poorer mental health in autistic women, but its relationship with suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and the role of autistic burnout and social support in this relationship, remain unclear. In this cross-sectional study, 213 autistic women with a formal diagnosis residing in Spain completed online measures of masking (CAT-Q), autistic burnout (AASPIRE Autistic Burnout Measure), suicidal thoughts and behaviours (SBQ-ASC), perceived social support (MSPSS) and anxiety (GAD-7). Data were analysed with hierarchical regression, structural equation modelling and conditional process analysis with bootstrap confidence intervals. Masking was consistently associated with higher autistic burnout, and perceived social support was associated with lower SBQ-ASC scores. Masking did not explain additional variance in SBQ-ASC scores after accounting for covariates and anxiety. The evidence for an indirect association between masking and SBQ-ASC scores through burnout was inconclusive, and social support did not moderate the masking–burnout association. These findings indicate that the relationships between masking, exhaustion and suicidality may be more complex than initially proposed, and highlight the need for longitudinal research and for support measures specifically adapted to autistic experiences.
